reports.text: CEB notice: planned power interruption in Bulathsinhala tomorrow 09:00-15:00 for line maintenance.
Call centre: 18 customers around Payagala say data is very slow and calls keep dropping.
Social media post: "heard the Minuwangoda tower is already fixed, the company van came" (unconfirmed).
NMS 06:00 | CRITICAL | MIN94 | RRU hardware fault, cells out of service
Bulletin 06:00 | Traffic police: Negombo to Minuwangoda route blocked, vehicles turned back

policy.evidence_rule: Authoritative evidence must be consistent; equally authoritative conflicts require confirmation. Recency alone does not verify a fact.
policy.on_crew_loss: Pause affected unfinished work and request operator review; preserve completed repairs.

finding.finding: Verified equipment fault at Minuwangoda (S17). No other verified operational facts.

The only resolved fault is verified equipment failure at S17; its grid power is available. EQ-S17 is catalogue-matched and C1–C4 have the required equipment skill. The road R17 is unknown, not confirmed blocked, so this does not justify deferring the repair. The reported Negombo–Minuwangoda blockage has no exact road-ID match and is not a basis to hold work. No unsafe or impossible action is established by the evidence.

questions.question: Is road R17 passable for crew access to S17?

finding.finding: V04 at S04 is the most consequential outage because it is policy-designated critical (weight 5), but the supplied state shows no equipment, power, or path fault there. V17 at S17 is down: its equipment is explicitly not OK, while grid power is OK and the route to the core is not shown impaired. All other services have no indicated outage in the resolved state. The Minuwangoda NMS snapshot identifies a critical RRU fault, consistent with S17 being down; the report that the route from Negombo to Minuwangoda is blocked is not mapped to a directory road ID, so its operational effect is unresolved.
